text: Refining D-0230 after #353's second review, which found that a neighbor could write the module's constant through an alias the scan for writes missed, so a passing proof stood for a module the runtime changed. The scan now covers every way an application source, tests included, can reach the function's module. A reference to the module, to a package above it, or to an application module whose imports bind one of those, through an import, a relative import, a module that imports it or a star import, may only read attributes. Refused: writing the module's attributes, or rebinding a package's attribute on the way to it, by assignment, augmented assignment or del; reading a special attribute other than __name__, __file__, __doc__, __path__, __all__ and __version__; and any other use, binding it to a name, passing it to a call (setattr, vars and patch.object included) and the rest, except that getattr, hasattr, setattr and delattr may take a package or module on the way to it by a constant naming something else in it. Reaching one of them by name is refused too: a string naming the module or something in it outside docstrings and annotations, as mock.patch('tasks.admission.LIMIT') has; sys.modules other than looked up, or tested with in, by a constant naming none of them; and importlib.import_module, importlib.__import__, __import__, pkgutil.resolve_name and pydoc.locate with a computed or relative name or one of theirs. So are reading __globals__ or f_globals anywhere, calling globals(), locals() or vars() in a source that holds one of them, a staged source the host's Python can't parse, and, when the module is a package's own __init__.py, a submodule named for something the function reads, which importing it would rebind. The module itself may star-import only Nagini's contracts, and the function may not read attributes of a builtin Nagini models, as str.maketrans, which needs a trusted contract as other builtins do. Still assumed, replacing D-0230's list: reflection the parse can't follow, as computed lookups on other objects, exec or eval outside the module, inspect, gc, frames and import hooks; that nothing outside the staged application writes the module's names, as a dependency or startup code could; that nothing replaces the builtins the function reads or the operations its trusted contracts stand for at run time, as patching them would; and Nagini's own model of the builtins it models and their exceptions.
